## Context

On macOS, `pytest -q tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py::test_windows_noop` reports `1 passed, 1 error`: the test body passes, then the autouse `_one_engine_root` teardown raises `NotImplementedError: cannot instantiate 'WindowsPath' on your system`.

## Root cause

`tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py:643` runs `monkeypatch.setattr(D.os, "name", "nt")`. `D.os` is the process-wide `os` module, so this rebinds `os.name` globally. `pathlib.Path.__new__` dispatches on the live `os.name`, so from that statement until `monkeypatch` undoes it, every `Path(...)` in the process yields `WindowsPath`, which refuses to instantiate on a POSIX host.

The undo does not happen before the guard runs. `pytest --setup-plan` shows `monkeypatch` is set up FIRST of the function-scoped fixtures, because several autouse fixtures request it; teardown is LIFO, so `monkeypatch` is torn down LAST. `_one_engine_root` tears down well before it, while `os.name` is still `nt`.

The guard's hot path is `foreign_engine_registrations` -> `_module_offences` -> `_foreign_root(str(file_name))` -> `engine_root_of`, and `engine_root_of` called `Path(path).resolve()`. On a `_foreign_root` cache miss for an unseen path, that is the construction that raises. The observed miss was `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/__init__.py`.

This is a class defect, not one test: the guard runs after every test in the suite, so any test that sets `os.name` breaks it.

## Fix

Make the guard's resolution string-based so it never depends on `os.name`. `os.path` and `os.sep` are bound at interpreter start and are unaffected by rebinding `os.name`, so `os.path.realpath` resolves identically while `Path` does not.

In `tests/_engine_path.py`: add a private `_engine_root_str(path)` resolving with `os.path.realpath(os.fspath(path))`, splitting on `os.sep`, scanning for the adjacent `_ENGINE_MARKER` pair, returning `str | None`. Reduce `engine_root_of` to wrapping it in `Path`, preserving its public signature. Change `_foreign_root` to return `str | None` from `_engine_root_str`, comparing against the canonical engine root as a string rather than re-running `engine_dir().resolve()` on every miss. Change the two `str(Path(...).resolve())` expressions in `_module_offences` to `os.path.realpath(...)`, which yields the same string.

After this the whole post-test guard path constructs no `Path`, so no part of it dispatches on `os.name`.

`_foreign_root` is private and its only caller is `_module_offences`, which tests it with `is not None`, so the return-type change reaches nothing else.

## Non-goals

The foreign-engine detection rule is unchanged: same marker pair, same canonical root, same offender set. `tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py` is not modified; the fix belongs in the guard so it holds for every future test that sets `os.name`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `pytest -q -p no:randomly tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py::test_windows_noop` reports `1 passed` with no error, where it currently reports `1 passed, 1 error`.

  **MET — reports exactly `1 passed in 1.84s`, no error line.**
- [x] `tests/_engine_path.py` defines `_engine_root_str` returning `str | None` and resolving via `os.path.realpath`.

  **MET — `:97` declares `-> str | None`; `:111` resolves via `os.path.realpath(os.fspath(path)).split(os.sep)`.**
- [x] `engine_root_of` still accepts `str | Path` and still returns `Path | None`.

  **MET — `:118`, signature unchanged.**
- [x] `_foreign_root` returns `str | None` and calls `_engine_root_str`, not `engine_root_of`.

  **MET — `:131` declares `-> str | None`; `:140` calls `_engine_root_str`.**
- [x] `_foreign_root` compares against `_canonical_engine_root_str()` rather than calling `engine_dir().resolve()`.

  **MET with a deliberate deviation. `:141` compares against the module constant `_CANONICAL_ENGINE_ROOT_STR` (`:75`), not a function. The constant resolves once at import with `os.path` only; a lazily-resolved function is computed on its first CALL, which for this guard can land inside the `nt` rebind window where `Path` is unusable. The AC's intent — stop reaching for `engine_dir().resolve()` — is met. Rationale recorded in the delivery comment.**
- [x] Neither `_module_offences` nor `_foreign_root` nor `_engine_root_str` constructs a `pathlib.Path`.

  **MET — `Path(` appears 4 times in the file: `:79`, `:85` (other functions), `:103` (docstring prose), `:127` (`engine_root_of`). None in the 3 named.**
- [x] A new test in `tests/unit/test_engine_root_convention.py` sets `os.name` to `nt` with `monkeypatch` and asserts `foreign_engine_registrations` returns without raising `NotImplementedError`.

  **MET — `:166` and `:190`.**
- [x] A new test in `tests/unit/test_engine_root_convention.py` sets `os.name` to `nt` with `monkeypatch` and asserts `engine_root_of` on a path outside any engine tree returns `None`.

  **MET — `:209`. This closes the real gap: under `nt` only `engine_root_of`'s None arm is reachable without raising, and that arm is what the teardown guard hits after each of ~19k tests.**
- [x] The existing `test_engine_root_of_ignores_paths_outside_any_engine_tree` passes unchanged, pinning that `engine_root_of` still returns `engine_dir()` for an engine file.

  **MET — `:161`, unchanged and passing.**
- [x] The existing foreign-copy detection test in `tests/unit/test_engine_root_convention.py` that builds a `shutil.copytree` duplicate still reports that copy as an offender.

  **MET — `:122` and `:132` both build a `copytree` duplicate via the `split_engine` fixture and still report it. Both pass.**
- [x] `pytest tests/unit/test_engine_root_convention.py` exits 0.

  **MET — `10 passed in 8.76s`, exit 0.**
- [x] `make verify` exits 0. [non-codebase]

  **MET [non-codebase] — proven by CI. Gerrit change 3013 carries `Verified +1` from the gating `pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.13)` cell. A local run cannot reach 0 here: `pypandoc-binary==1.17`'s macosx_11_0_arm64 wheel ships an x86_64 pandoc, failing 17 unrelated tests. Tracked as `9119-3f7b`; CI is linux and unaffected.**

## Delivery

Gerrit change 3013, merged as `6a873c9a96d2f4db3db10bd9a33108aa9709ee51`. Full per-criterion evidence is in the delivery comment.
